_about: DRAFT native-side trainer text for the Korean course, English learner (native/en/ko/trainer.draft.json). Extracted by script from the built app (globals + fn.toString()) and round-tripped against the live tables. Only two parts are authored, and both are marked: sound.rules ("_new": text the engine does not have) and the split of the V alternates into native (alt.V = the trailing English spellings) versus engine-neutral (alt._engineNeutral). Becomes native/<n>/ko/trainer.json; plan: docs/TRAINERS-PLAN.md. Keys are stable: Korean text where the engine table is keyed by Korean, else a fixed English slug. Slots are %1..%9 (positional; braces are forbidden in native text by validate.js). Fields starting with _ are notes, ignored by assembly.

hangul._src: Hangul reading drill (features.script). app.html: "// Hangul drill word lists" (const WORDS_CV / MEAN_ADD / MEAN / WORDS_F), "// Hangul drill" (const L / V / T, answersFor, hangulItem), renderHangulQ, renderHangulPick.

mean._src: MEAN (incl. MEAN_ADD), keyed by the Korean drill word, in WORDS_CV then WORDS_F order. Shown after each answer as " · gloss". Every WORDS_CV/WORDS_F word has one.

alt._src: typed-answer alternates appended after the engine's canonical RR + neutral variants (const V [2] trailing items; answersFor li.push('sh')). Order is significant: [canonical, ...engine neutral, ...these].

ui._src: renderHangulQ / renderHangulPick literals. Bare words and the HTML hint are concatenated into the DOM, so they live here, not in the i18n keys.
ui.empty: Type the sound in English letters (e.g. ga), or type the Hangul itself.

onboard._src: renderOnboard() (Korean-script onboarding, shown when features.script). Rendered by a trainer function, so it lives in TRAINER.onboard (plan §2.6); started = toast with the first deck label as %1.
onboard.title: 안녕하세요 👋 Two quick questions
onboard.goal: What do you want Korean for?

gloss._src: Sentence breakdown (🔍 break it down, Build drill feedback, Words from dialogues). app.html "// rule-based breakdown of a Korean sentence": const PART / ENDS / QW / CONN / COUNT and the literals inside breakdown(). PART and ENDS ORDER is match logic and stays in the engine (target half); native files are keyed maps. NUMS (digits) is language-neutral.

tpl._src: breakdown() inline strings; %1.. = Korean stem / particle / gloss in the order the engine passes them
tpl.question: %1 (question word)

build._src: Build drill (features.script today; gloss-gated in the plan). buildSentences() hard-coded story/negation pairs (Korean → English), renderBuildQ literals. The Korean moves to target/ko (course.json build[]); the gloss stays native.

extra.먼저 카페에 갔어요: First we went to a café
extra.그다음에 영화를 봤어요: After that we watched a movie
extra.지난 주말에 뭐 했어요: What did you do last weekend

numbers._src: Numbers drill (features.numbers). numItem() hint literals, its counter pick list, renderNumberQ literals. Kinds: price,price,time,phone,floor,count,age,minutes

hint.time: time (native hour, Sino minutes) — type like 3:30

sound._src: Sound-change drill + card pronunciation note (features.sound). pronounce() rules.add(...) names are KOREAN and are what the engine shows today; the engine has no explanation text. The "gloss" values below are NEW (not in the engine), condensed from lesson sound-changes (native/en/ko/lessons/sound-changes.html) so translators have a source; sound.showGloss=false keeps en-ko rendering the Korean name only (byte-identical); packs set it true; WP8 decides for en-ko.

rules.받침 → %1: final consonant said as %1 (only 7 finals survive)
rules.ㄴ 첨가 → ㄹㄹ: ㄴ is added, then becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ
rules.연음: linking: the final consonant slides into the next syllable
rules.구개음화: ㄷ / ㅌ before 이 are said ㅈ / ㅊ
rules.격음화: ㅎ next to ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ makes them airy ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ
rules.비음화: nasal: ㅂ ㄷ ㄱ soften to ㅁ ㄴ ㅇ before ㄴ / ㅁ
rules.유음화: ㄴ meets ㄹ: both become ㄹ
rules.받침 중화: final consonant neutralised to its basic sound
rules.ㅢ → 이: ㅢ not at the start of a word is said 이

register._src: Polite ↔ casual drill (features.register). renderRegisterQ() literals; the pairs themselves are target-side (course.json pairs, 36).
register.whyPolite: casual → polite: add 요 (or the honorific verb)

conj._src: Verb conjugator (features.conj). cjHTML() row labels keyed by conj() result field, conj() irregular.push() tags, renderGrammar() panel literals.

ui.empty: Enter a dictionary form ending in 다.
ui.title: Verb conjugator
ui.tryLine: Try 가다 · 먹다 · 하다 · 마시다 · 예쁘다 · 듣다 · 돕다 · 살다 · 모르다

quiz._src: renderQuizQ: the "Why" line shown on a wrong answer in grammar-kind decks (deck regex → KINDS.grammar in the plan).

koui._src: const KOUI ("rom · gloss" tooltips that koTips() puts on Korean UI words). The romanisation is target-side (computed or stored in target/ko); only the gloss is native.

strokes._src: strokeSVG() replay button, drawn on card backs in every course (STROKES paths are language-neutral; features.strokes is never read by the engine).
